use_case_name: Add Files to an Existing Archive

claims.content: The User aims to add selected files or folders to an existing archive.

scope_contract.goal_statement: The User aims to add selected files or folders to an existing archive.
scope_contract.canonical_success_scenario: The User selects one or more files or folders and adds them to an existing archive using an available add action in the file manager interface.
scope_contract.start_boundary: An existing archive is available, and the User has identified files or folders to add.
scope_contract.success_boundary: The selected files or folders have been added to the existing archive.
in_scope_actions: Select files or folders to add
Invoke the add action via the Add button, context menu, or drag-and-drop
Add the selected files or folders to the existing archive
variant_dimensions: Add method: Add button, context menu, or drag-and-drop

claims.content: User
An existing archive is available for updating.
The files or folders to be added exist on storage devices accessible through the file manager interface.
The User selects one or more objects (files or archives) to add to an archive from the file manager interface and initiates the action.

missing_aspects: Evidence supports adding objects to 'an archive' or 'the current archive', but does not explicitly restrict this specific trigger to 'existing' archives only (creation is also implied by other methods in source).

Evidence lists multiple initiation methods ('Add' button, context menu, drag-and-drop), whereas the claim implies a generic 'initiates the add action' without specifying the mechanism, which is acceptable, but the restriction to 'existing' archives makes it unsupported.

claims.content: The User selects one or more files or folders in the file manager interface.
The User invokes the add action using one of the available methods in the file manager interface: the Add button or context menu.
The system adds the selected files or folders to the archive.

covered_aspect_ids: Step-by-step normal interaction sequence for adding files to an existing archive
missing_aspects: Evidence for 'drag-and-drop' as a method within the file manager interface is not present in the cited cards; EC-MF-001 describes drag-and-drop adding objects *to* the interface (implying an external source), whereas this step implies invoking an action *within* the interface.

The cited cards support adding to 'an existing archive' (EC-MF-003) or 'the current archive' (EC-MF-001), but do not explicitly restrict the outcome to only 'existing' archives (creation of new archives is also a documented capability in the broader context, though not in these specific snippets). Removing 'existing' ensures strict fidelity to the provided text which focuses on the action of adding rather than the state of the target.

claims.content: Diverges from Step 2: Instead of invoking the add action with the Add button or context menu, the User drags files or folders from the search dialog and drops them into the archiving layout to add them to the archive (context menu only).

Diverges from Step 2: Instead of invoking the add action with the Add button or context menu, the User drags and drops objects onto the file manager interface while browsing the existing archive; the objects are added to the current archive if the archive format allows modifications.

missing_aspects: Alternative successful paths for adding files to an existing archive

claims.content: At Step 3, if the selected storage space is read-only or the User lacks permissions to write to the destination, the system prevents adding the selected files or folders to the archive; the addition does not occur.

At Step 3, if the existing archive format does not support modification (for example, a read-only or immutable compressed format), the system prevents adding the selected files or folders and may display an error message indicating incompatibility; the addition does not occur.

At Step 3, if an error occurs during file addition, the system displays a dialog with options to retry, cancel, or view details; no automatic recovery is performed without User intervention. The User can choose one of these documented options.

At Step 3, if an error occurs during file addition and the 'Backend binaries user interface' setting is 'Keep open only if needed (errors, list, test...)', the backend interface remains open for User inspection.

missing_aspects: Documented exit or continuation after addition is prevented by a read-only destination or insufficient write permissions.
Documented exit or continuation after addition is prevented by an archive format that does not support modification.
Outcome of choosing retry, cancel, or view details after an add error.
Documented continuation or exit after the backend interface remains open for error inspection.
Exception branch for OS drag-and-drop incompatibility cannot be mapped to a main-flow step because main_flow does not include drag-and-drop add invocation.
Documented exit or continuation after addition is prevented by a read-only destination or insufficient permissions.
Outcome of the retry, cancel, or view-details choices after an add error.
Explicit prevention conditions for modifying archives.
Specific error messages for add failure.

claims.content: The selected files or folders have been added to the existing archive, and the existing archive has been updated with the added content.
The updated archive retains the same name and storage location as it had before the update.
The original files or folders that were added retain their content and name and remain saved in the same space of the computer system where they were initially stored.
The system displays a 'Job successfully completed' message with statistics including Input size, Output size (with compression percentage), and Time elapsed.

claims.content: The User aims to add selected files or folders to an existing archive.
An existing archive is available for updating.

The User selects one or more objects (files or archives) to add to an archive from the file manager interface and initiates the action.
The User selects one or more files or folders in the file manager interface.

Diverges from Step 2: Instead of invoking the add action with the Add button or context menu, the User drags files or folders from the search dialog and drops them into the archiving layout to add them to the archive (context menu only).

At Step 3, if the selected storage space is read-only or the User lacks permissions to write to the destination, the system prevents adding the selected files or folders to the archive; the addition does not occur.

At Step 3, if an error occurs during file addition and the 'Backend binaries user interface' setting is 'Keep open only if needed (errors, list, test...)', the backend interface remains open for User inspection.
